strings.title: JSON_VAULT
strings.subtitle: Skill: unpacking JSON into columns
strings.briefing:
Each order's details arrived as a block of JSON text in one column: {"customer": {"id": 20, "name": "Ben Okafor"}, "total": 88.57}. You cannot filter or sum text.

Flatten it into real columns: order_id, customer_id, customer_name and total. The payload column goes away.

In pandas, json.loads turns the text into dictionaries and pd.json_normalize flattens them. In SQL, json_extract(text, '$.path') reaches inside.

In Python, finish with df as the reshaped table. In SQL, build a table named result and that is what gets judged.
strings.task: The payload column holds JSON text. Unpack it into normal columns: order_id, customer_id, customer_name and total. The payload column must disappear.

starterCode.python:
# df has 80 rows: order_id and a JSON text column, payload.
df['payload'].head(3).tolist()
starterCode.sql:
-- data has 80 rows: order_id and a JSON text column, payload.
SELECT order_id, payload FROM data LIMIT 3;

python: Parse each text value first: df['payload'].apply(json.loads). You will need import json.
pd.json_normalize(parsed, sep='_') flattens nested keys into customer_id and customer_name.

import json
flat = pd.json_normalize(df['payload'].apply(json.loads), sep='_')
df = pd.concat([df[['order_id']], flat], axis=1)
sql: json_extract(payload, '$.total') reads a field. Nested fields use dots: '$.customer.name'.
Select one json_extract per output column and give each an alias.

CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT order_id, json_extract(payload,'$.customer.id') AS customer_id, json_extract(payload,'$.customer.name') AS customer_name, json_extract(payload,'$.total') AS total FROM data;
